report.source_text: Routine blood examination showed a normal haemoglobin level (119 g/L), normal white cell count (5.85×109/L) but severe thrombocytopenia (3000/mm3). Peripheral smear showed normal morphology of red blood cells, leucocytes but significantly reduced platelets. No blast cells or atypical cells were seen. Liver and kidney function tests were within normal limits. Coagulation profile (prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and international normalised ratio (INR)) was normal. Fibrinogen level was slightly elevated (411 mg/dL; range 162–401 mg/dL) but serum triglyceride (55 mg/dL) and serum ferritin (350 ng/mL) were within normal limits. Pro-calcitonin levels were also within normal limits.

report.source_text: She had completed 4 weeks of induction phase with vincristine (1.5 mg/m2; once weekly), L-asparaginase (10 000 IU/m2), oral prednisolone (60 mg/m2/day) and intrathecal methotrexate (6 mg; once weekly). After achieving complete remission, she was started on consolidation phase for 4 weeks with vincristine (1.5 mg/m2), 6-mercaptopurine (75 mg/m2/day) and intrathecal methotrexate (6 mg; once weekly). After the consolidation phase, she was started on maintenance therapy. Five days into her maintenance therapy, she started to develop high-grade fever with cold and coryza. RT-PCR of the oropharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2. In view of this, her chemotherapy was immediately withheld and she was managed symptomatically. Her symptoms subsided over the next 5 days. Routine blood examination was within normal limits at the time. She was planned to be restarted on maintenance chemotherapy after 14 days of recovery from COVID-19. After the initiation of maintenance phase with intrathecal methotrexate and oral 6-mercaptopurine, she was discharged home to review after 2 weeks for complete blood count.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A five-and-a-half-year-old girl with a history of B-cell ALL on maintenance therapy presented with reddish-purple spots on her neck, shoulder, arms, and legs, 22 days after recovering from SARS-CoV-2 infection. Initial blood work revealed severe thrombocytopenia (3000/mm3) with normal hemoglobin and white cell count, and a peripheral smear showing significantly reduced platelets but no blast cells. Coagulation profile was normal. A bone marrow aspiration cytology was performed to rule out ALL relapse, which showed normocellular bone marrow with increased megakaryopoiesis and no blast cells, consistent with ITP. Initial treatment included platelet transfusions for active cutaneous bleeding. She was then administered intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) and oral prednisolone, but her platelet count remained low (<10,000/mm3) with new petechiae and oral mucosal bleeding, requiring further platelet transfusions. Subsequently, thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor agonists (romiplostim and eltrombopag) were initiated. Her platelet counts improved to 24,000/mm3 within two weeks and further increased to 157,000/mm3. After a 4-week hospital stay, she was discharged on tapering prednisolone and eltrombopag. On follow-up, eltrombopag and prednisolone were stopped, and she was well with normal blood counts, allowing for the resumption of her maintenance chemotherapy for B-cell ALL.
